summary.headline: Sheela Foam Q4 FY26 consolidated core EBITDA rose 90% YoY to INR121 crore at an 11.5% margin, with first-ever dividend of 20% recommended.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 24% YoY to INR1,050 crore, and FY26 revenue rose 11% to INR3,821 crore, with management citing record foam production, top line and EBITDA. Core EBITDA for FY26 was INR414 crore (10.8% margin, up 261 bps), and consolidated PAT was INR92 crore in Q4 (about 7x YoY) and INR161 crore for FY26. Net debt fell INR156 crore in FY26, and the Board recommended a first-ever 20% dividend. Management flagged raw material (TDI, polyol) volatility from the Middle East conflict, saying prices were 25-35% higher on average, and that pass-through has largely been taken.

financial_highlights.value: INR161 crore; INR144 crore earned in H2

segments.name: Mattress (India, Sleepwell + Kurlon)
segments.commentary: Volumes grew 13% YoY in Q4 and 12% for FY26; value grew 13% in Q4 and 10% for FY26. Around 600 net new showrooms were added in FY26.

segments.name: Foam (India)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 volume grew 34% and value 36%, aided by better price realisation. FY26 volume grew 18% and value 14%. Management said B2B and comfort foam grew upwards of 15% annually.

segments.name: U2O (unorganised to organised, small-town India)
segments.commentary: Served through 8,400 dealers across over 5,000 towns in 24 states. FY26 volume grew 65% and value 111%, helped by a higher-priced second model and price increases.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Brand.com sales grew 136% YoY and platform sales 39% YoY in FY26; management cited a 52% value growth figure in Q&A.

segments.name: Australia (Joyce)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR422 crore with EBITDA margin of 10%, up almost 400 bps from FY25, driven by yield programmes, price renegotiation and supply-chain restructuring.

segments.name: Spain
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR391 crore with EBITDA margin of 10.4%, against 8.4% in FY25. Management sees a stable 30-32% gross margin range.

segments.name: Furlenco
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR370 crore (over 60% growth) and PAT of close to INR60 crore versus INR3 crore in FY25. Company holds about 43% fully diluted; FY27 revenue target is about INR500 crore.

guidance_outlook: Targeted growth of 15%+ over the medium term, expected to be higher given raw material-led price increases; management is aiming for a 3-5 year horizon to become a full product player.
Management believes core EBITDA margin is in an 11-12% range and can move higher with growth; Q1-Q2 FY27 margin impact from raw materials expected at no more than 50-100 bps.
FY27 standalone depreciation guided at INR140-145 crore on a consolidated basis, roughly INR35 crore per quarter.
FY27 capex guided at INR125-150 crore including maintenance, debottlenecking, marketing capex for new stores, across India, Australia and Spain.
Consolidated finance cost guided at about INR50 crore for FY27 (about INR35 crore interest plus INR15 crore other charges).
India debt of about INR300 crore expected to be repaid in 1-1.5 years; Australia and Spain debt of about INR350 crore is self-liquidating.
Remaining Kurlon synergies of about INR40 crore (out of INR250 crore total) depend on new machines that are delayed about 1.5 quarters; installation expected by mid or end of Q1 FY27.
Furlenco IPO decision to be taken in the next 3-4 months; listing expected in about one year or later.
Dividend of 20% for FY26 recommended, subject to shareholder approval; first dividend in company history.
Pillows (about INR100 crore market) to be treated as a separate category going forward; brand.com and U2O remain focus areas.
Hope to cross 100 integrated Furlenco-Sheela stores in FY27 (currently over 40).
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at INR125-150 crore including maintenance, debottlenecking to support volume growth of about 15% in FY26, and new store marketing capex.
Greater Noida foaming machine has run for 22 years, producing about 25,000 tonnes of foam per annum; management cited 40-50 year asset lives in the depreciation policy change.
A 500 kW solar plant is operational at Jabalpur, with over 1,000 kW of additional solar under progress at other manufacturing locations.
New imported machines for malleable-fibre comfort-layer production are under installation, delayed about 1.5 quarters, to support INR40 crore synergy.
demand_pricing: Raw material pricing: TDI and polyol rose 25-35% on average. Polyol was about INR120/kg in January, peaked near INR220, and is now around INR180-200. TDI is currently around INR275 (GNFC price); management cites a 5-year average of about INR240.
Pass-through is strong in B2C and industrial foam and partial in B2B. Management said the price increase has already been taken and margins will not be hit going forward.
Q4 volume spike was partly from smaller foam players exiting due to supply constraints, and from share gains in comfort and B2B foam. Management said no major channel stocking occurred.
TDI supply: GNFC plant shut for technical and gas reasons, so the company added a new hedging supplier (Korea, Japan and China sources) and avoided stock-outs at higher prices.
Management said organised share is rising relative to unorganised, reversing the trend of the last couple of years.
Marketing spend for FY26 is around 4.5% of sales, similar to last year.

qa_highlights.question: Are margins under pressure in Q1-Q2 FY27 given higher-cost raw material inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Gupta said price changes flow through in 10-15 days and inventory costs match, so the gross margin impact is limited to about 50-100 bps. Volume growth, given a 30%+ contribution margin, should support EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why is U2O value growth (111%) far above volume growth (65%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Rakesh Chahar said a higher-priced second model was introduced and both models saw price increases. U2O margins are between offline and e-commerce margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the change in depreciation policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Gupta said the written-down method front-loaded depreciation (70-75% in the first 3-4 years) for assets with 40-50 year lives, so the policy was realigned to useful life.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Australia and Spain margins, and is a sale still under consideration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees Spain gross margins at 30-32% and Australian margins up about 4-5 points on a normal basis. The target is 10-12% EBITDA. Rahul Gautam said the company is open to a sale but is not actively pursuing one.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Furlenco plans and how is ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Gupta said the company holds about 43% fully diluted and invested about INR430 crore, with ROCE of 30-35%. FY27 revenue target is about INR500 crore; an IPO is considered once a threshold size is reached, possibly in about a year.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the remaining synergy is pending?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Gupta said INR190-200 crore of the INR250 crore synergy is achieved, with INR40 crore pending on new machines that are delayed about 1.5 quarters and expected to be installed by mid or end of Q1 FY27.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility (TDI, polyol) from the Middle East conflict and GNFC supply disruption; management admits pricing is hard to predict.
Sustainability of the Q4 volume spike, which was partly from competitors exiting; whether customers stay after supply normalises.
Delayed INR40 crore synergy from new machines; watch whether it is installed by end of Q1 FY27.
Depreciation policy change flatters reported profit; compare with peers on a like-for-like basis.
Furlenco IPO timing and valuation, and integration of its stores into the network.
Management did not disclose the U2O volume share of total mattress volumes; a follow-up was promised.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, margins and the dividend, with explicit targets. Cautious and somewhat evasive on raw material pricing trajectory and on the timing of any sale of the international business.
key_quotes: This marks the first dividend recommended by the company since listing or for that matter, forever.
We are a 30% plus contribution margin business.
So polyols should be around INR120 plus and TDI should be around INR240 or something like that.
It will not revert to 28%, 29%, which we had seen in the past.

adds.what: New imported machines for malleable-fibre comfort-layer production (support INR40 crore Kurlon synergy)
Over 1,000 kW additional solar under progress at manufacturing locations (energy, not production capacity)

growth.why: Management targets 15%+ medium-term growth (expected higher given raw-material-led price rises) with FY27 capex of INR125-150 crore and Furlenco FY27 revenue target of ~INR500 crore, but few concrete new-capacity numbers were given beyond the delayed comfort-layer machines (~1.5 quarters late) and the Greater Noida line already running.
